plan.english: Dawn grew bright. Then the man stood up and went to his own field. Joining the two cattle to the plough, he drove them. Then he ploughed with the plough, and the sun was high. Sweating, he grew tired. Then he cried out to Sky: 'Father Sky, give water to my field!' Father Sky heard him, and it rained, and the cloud went away. When it was getting dark, he led them to the house. Then he was asleep.

The wheat grew large. Then the father and the mother went to the field. He was cutting off the ears of grain, and she carried the load. The two sons dried the ears. Then they put the load on the wagon, and two swift horses pulled it. Then she crushed the wheat. Eating it, they rejoiced. 'Mother Earth, you gave us grain!'

When Dawn grew bright, the man led the cattle out of the cow-stall. Then they went to the pasture. They ate, and they drank. When the sun was high, he sat down under a tree. When it was getting dark, he drove them on to the cow-stall. Then he was asleep, and the dog guarded them.

At dawn the daughter went to the enclosure. Then she sat down nearby and milked the sheep. The mother was awake, and she said: 'Daughter, bring water!' Then she stood up and carried it to the house. Having drunk, she was satisfied.

When it was getting dark, the wolf crept toward the enclosure. The flock trembled in fear. The dog heard it, and he cried out. Then the man woke up. Seizing his spear, he caught sight of the wolf at the door. Then he killed it. Then he lay down again.
The mother took wool. Then she twisted it. She was sitting at the door. Then, stretching the wool, she wove. When Dawn grew bright, she clothed her son with it. He rejoiced.
The man put the bronze in the fire. Then the bronze melted. Then, seizing it, he kept hitting it. He made a spear, and it was pointed. Then a stranger came and bought it. He gave wheat in exchange.

The two brothers were cutting trees. Then they placed them on the wagon. Then they set them upright and built the house. Then they covered it, and they made a door. Their sister carried wheat inside. The house stood, and they dwelt in it.

The man went along the road to a friend. Two swift horses carried him. Then the wheel broke. He held the two horses and set it upright. Then he came to the friend. The master was standing at the door, and he rejoiced. Then he led him in.

A cloud was appearing, and it rained. The sheep trembled in fear. The man led them into the enclosure. The ram went ahead, and they followed. Then he sat down at the door. Then it grew bright, and they came out.

When it was getting dark, a stranger stole two horses. Then the man woke up and did not catch sight of them. 'Son, wake up! Who took them?' 'The stranger took them.' The dog tracked them, and the man followed it. There they saw them. The stranger was afraid, and he went away. Then he drove them home.

The brother and the sister went to the water, and it was deep. The fish were swimming in it. Then the brother killed a fish with the spear. Then the sister cooked it. They ate, and they were satisfied. Then they sat down.

The daughter was working in the field. Then a bear came out from the trees. She was afraid, and she cried out. Her brother heard her, and seizing his spear, he came to her. The bear caught sight of him and went away. Then she rejoiced.
Fire was burning in the house. Then the master woke up and said: 'Son, wake up!' Then they carried water, and the fire died. The house did not burn. Then they sat down and drank.

A man came to the house, who led ten sheep. The master was standing at the door. 'Give me your daughter!' 'What is the bride-price?' 'The bride-price is so many.' Then the master gave his daughter to him. They drank, and they rejoiced.

The wheel of the sun climbed up. Then the flock came out, and the men were at work. Then the wheel of the sun sank down, and the moon grew bright. Then they sat down inside. They were asleep. The stars grew bright above the house.
'Who is standing at the door?' 'I am a thirsty stranger. Make me sip!' 'Come in!' 'Are you the master of the house?' 'I am the master.' 'Sit down and eat wheat!'

'Eat in my house, and drink there!' 'What is on the table?' 'Wheat is on the table, and the cook cooked a ram.' 'Is it good?' 'It is good.' 'I eat it, and I am satisfied with it.' 'Let us drink again!' 'May the gods give you good things.'
'Dear one, I am buying the horse.' 'What is the price?' 'Give me four cattle!' 'I give you two cattle and a ram.' 'Let us make a pledge.' 'Lead the horse and rejoice with it!'

'Mother, where is father?' 'He is in the cow-stall.' 'Make me sip!' 'Son, drink!' 'What are you weaving?' 'I am weaving wool.' 'I caught sight of a wolf!' 'Where did you catch sight of it?' 'I caught sight of it at the door.' 'Do not tremble at it! Sit down.'

'Dear one, where is the flock?' 'It is under the tree.' 'Have you seen the wolf?' 'I have seen it near the enclosure.' 'Let us guard the flock. You go with the dog. I go there.' 'Father Sky, protect us!'

'Son, hold the plough! Join the two cattle to the plough.' 'How do I drive them?' 'Drive them with a word, and do not hit them! When you plough with the plough, put grain in the ploughed field.' 'I have grown tired from the work.' 'He who ploughs with the plough has good fame.'

title: Brother and sister at the fire

plan.english: 'Sister, is the fire burning?' 'It is burning, and the water is boiling.' 'Brother, cook the grain!' 'I am preparing it.' 'Who is eating the wheat?' 'The dog is eating.' 'Do not hit him! He is dear.'
'Sister, whose wool is this?' 'It is my wool. I took it.' 'Your wool is long. What are you weaving?' 'I am weaving for the king.' 'May the king become warm! May you not become tired from the work.'
'Did you make the spear?' 'I made it. Look at it!' 'It is long, and it is pointed. What am I giving you?' 'Give me wheat!' 'I give you wheat in exchange.' 'May it give you good fame!'
'Dear one, my wheel broke. Do you have one?' 'I have one.' 'Give it to me, and I give you a ram in exchange.' 'Take it and go!' 'You are a giver of good things.'

'Dear one, have you seen the sheep?' 'I have not seen her.' 'She is gone. Did the wolf take her?' 'I do not know that. Let us seek her. You go to the cow-stall, and I go to the door.' 'I found her under the tree!' 'Is she alive?' 'She is alive.'

title: The way to the king's house

plan.english: 'Man, which road goes to the king's house?' 'The road goes there. Go through the trees, and then you see it.' 'Is the road long?' 'The road is not long.' 'May the god protect you!'
'Brother, what is fame?' 'It is a famous name.' 'Who has fame?' 'He who slays the bear has great fame.' 'Did you slay a bear?' 'I slew it, and my name is known.' 'May my name be known!'

'Daughter, where does the sun go?' 'It goes under the earth.' 'Who carries it?' 'Two swift horses carry it.' 'When it gets dark, what grows bright?' 'The moon grows bright.' 'Does the sun see us?' 'It sees us.' 'Father, I am not afraid.'

'Where are you going?' 'I am going to the king's house.' 'What are you carrying?' 'I am carrying wool.' 'The road is long. Let us speak together.' 'Who is the king?' 'The king has great fame, and his name is known.'

title: The daughter-in-law and the man at the door

plan.english: 'Daughter-in-law, a man is standing at the door. Do not leave him. Cook a sheep!' 'Which one shall I cook?' 'Cook the ram! Set the table!' 'I am setting it.'
Crush the wheat. Carry fire into the house, and put water on it. When it boils, put the wheat into it. Set the table. Sit down at the table and eat wheat.
Lead the two cattle out of the cow-stall. Join them to the plough. Do not hit them. Drive them with a word. When they are tired, make them lie down. Then drive them on to the cow-stall.

Wake up at dawn. Drive the flock out. Lead the dog along beside you. Do not lie down. Look at it, and listen to him. If a wolf comes, cry out. Kill it with the spear. Then drive the flock into the enclosure. Father Sky, may you protect it!
When it has rained, plough the field. Put the grain in the ploughed field, and cover it with earth. Guard the ploughed field. Do not leave it. Mother Earth, may the grain grow large!

If a guest is standing at the door, stand up and go to the door. Lead him into the house. Give him wheat. Seat him at the table. Do not kill him. He is dear to the god. When it grows bright, let him go.
Take wool from the ram. Dry it. Twist it, and stretch it. Do not break it. Weave it. Clothe yourself with it. May the wool warm you!
Guard the fire. Do not let it die. When it is getting dark, cover it. When it grows bright, heat the house. Fire, protect us!
At dawn go to the enclosure. Sit down beside the sheep. Do not cry out. Do not hit them. Speak to them. Milk them. Carry the load inside.
